articles.post_title: Why use CURRENT_TIMESTAMP on a field that record date/time?
articles.excerpt: On a TIMESTAMP field that records date and time when inserting a new record, it is encouraged to use as a DEFAULT value, the CURRENT_TIMESTAMP constant. Why? Because when inserting a new row in the table for the date and time field there is no need to specifically add its value, either by creating it from PHP code with the Date/ Time functions or with MySQL function NOW() ALTER TABLE `user` CHANGE `dateCreated` `dateCreated` TIMESTAMP NOT  DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP; CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is also a solution for  updating date and time fields.
